zulake

zulake is an R package that opens a Delta Lake table where it is stored and returns what the table’s log records as base data frames.

  • It replays the log in R, as the Delta Lake protocol prescribes: versions, commits, live files with their partition values and statistics, deletion vectors, schema and the changes between versions.
  • It reads the data too, ruling out files by partition values and statistics before reading any of them.
  • Tables can be on local disk, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 or Azure Blob Storage, with a bearer token from a function you supply.
  • A table that needs a feature zulake does not support is refused by name, never read wrong.

Installation

zulake is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zulake")

Usage

The package ships a small table of orders, partitioned by region. Open it, and list the files that can hold an order from the EU over 1000:

library(zulake)

tbl <- lake_open(system.file("extdata", "orders", package = "zulake"))
lake_files(tbl, filter = region == "EU" & amount > 1000)[c("path", "num_records")]
#>                          path num_records
#> 1 region=EU/part-0002.parquet           3
#> 2 region=EU/part-0008.parquet           2

zulake also lists the table’s history and changes, and reads its rows; Get started shows each of them.

Learn more

  • Get started: open a table, inspect its log, read it with a filter, and read from Azure.
  • Reference: every function, the data frames they return and the errors they raise.
  • Changelog: what each version changed.

zulake reads tables and does not write them; to write one, use the Python deltalake package or Spark.
